BEYOND FLOATING POINT

Infinity is a direction.

The image is the actual Mandelbrot set: we repeatedly calculate z² + c for each point and color how quickly it escapes.

The journey descends into an exact self-similar boundary point near Seahorse Valley. It satisfies z₂₅(c) = z₂₀(c), with a repelling period-five cycle. As more digits become necessary, a background worker refines that same algebraic point with arbitrary-precision arithmetic. The destination never drifts into empty space.

Deep zoom uses recursive cycle folding: the repeating orbit is composed by recursive squaring, carrying its scale and rotation into the next local frame. The reference table stays at 26 points and the GPU keeps a fixed work budget as depth increases. Every frame is still computed from the Mandelbrot equation; there are no prerecorded images or zoom resets.

Scroll or pinch to adjust zoom without stopping the journey. Drag to pause and explore freely; press Play to return to the automatic descent at your current depth. The circular reset button restarts from the beginning. Press H to hide the interface.

No physical computer can finish an infinite computation. There is no preset zoom endpoint; available memory, GPU accuracy, and computation time determine practical depth. Resolution adapts to your GPU, and hidden tabs stop rendering.
